newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela seals oil spill tanker, slick no larger.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela seals oil spill tanker, slick no larger.

text.p: Engineers sealed the remaining leaks on a Greek oil tanker anchored off Venezuela's northwestern coast Wednesday and environmental damage from the oil spill appeared to be diminishing, officials said.
"They've just closed the final holes," said Danny Romero, spokesman for Maraven, a subsidiary of state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela.

The Greek-flagged Nissos Amorgos, carrying 476,000 barrels of heavy Venezuelan crude bound for Italy, ran aground on Friday in a shipping channel at the mouth of Lake Maracaibo, spilling about 25,000 barrels, industry officials said.
The spill grew to 60,000 barrels when the ship was moved east for repairs, the Venezuelan Navy said.
Despite the large size of the spill, damage has been limited to about 11 miles (17.5 km) of sandy coastline on the western flank of the Gulf of Venezuela.

"It's a bit better today, they have collected a lot of material," Lenin Herrera, president of the Lake Maracaibo Conservation Institute (ICLAM), told Reuters in a brief telephone conversation as he flew over the affected area.
About 500 men continued to shovel oil-stained sand off the polluted coastline Wednesday, he said.
The Nissos Amorgos, which was bound for Italy, remained at anchor about 14 miles off the Paraguana peninsula in western Venezuela.
